objective: Take up backlog B52, given the go-ahead by the coordinator on 2026-11-09 (G1 with G5): under the doubling law, does a schedule whose rings hear each other at a doubling lag always leave a stage unbalanced within boundedly many doublings? A pre-registered census of open and open-plus-copy schedules at g = 2 and 3, reading at each doubling whether rings hear each other and whether the stage is balanced, with the bound frozen before reading; then a proof attempt.
status: Complete 2026-11-09 (frozen census, H refuted): isolation is sufficient but not necessary for balance under the doubling law. At g = 3 open births doubling every 2 and every 4 lags keep every stage balanced while rings hear each other, to 24 x 24 (reading further to 48 x 48 pending); at g = 2 every hearing schedule fails within two doublings and P = 1, 3, 7 isolate and stay balanced. The exclusion read by DOUBLE-BALANCE-20261109-001 and BIRTH-RULE-20261109-001 holds at g = 2 only (Narrowing). Recommendation Continue: distance in the g = 3 growing plane (B53).
stop_rule: Stop at a proof of a bound, at a schedule that stays balanced while its rings hear each other to the size limit, or at the census's bound with the proof left open.
title: Is isolation necessary for balance under doubling?
